svg.text: Ballast Drill T03k: take C (hoses) on an unbroken plate wall (2D game-view sketches)

Liam on T03j: "Hoses but the pipe connections edge over hangs the wall"; "Close the bays"; south "Flush with wall"; bore "0.32, vanilla". 64 px a tile at 1x, the game's camera; footprint corners ticked.
Changed from take C: the plate wall unbroken at 0.85 round all four faces (no bays; corners open, legs as before); the south face out from 2.496 to 2.74, the end rings flush in it;

hoses 0.32 (were 0.26); each gooseneck over its own fitting, its cast body 0.08 inside the face; the hoses no longer lift over bay corners (no short bridge needed); each ends in a cast boss on the plate
against the shoulder (a 0.32 nozzle no longer fits the shoulder's 0.16 side clear of the landed ring). The chute through a port in the wall: recommended, a question (below).

Hoses (plan; N/S keyed by the fitting's side of x, E/W by north/south of centre): E+: 0.79 long, turns 12 deg; E-: 0.93 long, turns 21 deg; N+: 0.90 long, turns 73 deg; N-: 0.89 long, turns 72 deg;
S+: 1.06 long, turns 30 deg; S-: 1.05 long, turns 29 deg; W+: 0.79 long, turns 12 deg; W-: 0.93 long, turns 21 deg.

Clearance, worst over all 8: hose to bastions 0.03, guide feet 0.35, shoulder 0.06; lowest hose bottom 0.03 over the plate; nozzle tip 0.08 outside the ring's landing radius; gooseneck body 0.08 inside its face, 0.06 from the bastions;
off the plate 0; over a bay: none (closed); never turns back (worst step away from its end -0.0106).

Port 0.86 wide, 0.30 high, in a steel frame. The spec's chute
unchanged (ground level, set into the face, mouth flush,
nothing over the roofline): the plate bridges it as a lintel. The body
never turns, so every face has the port; the three the ore does not leave
by are shut by a flush bolted hatch (today's bay hatches, stood up).
From the camera the S port is seen; N, E and W ports are not (edge on or
behind), so the drive sits on the plate top over the mouth to show the
output face in every direction (turns with the chute).
South: the face is 0.24 further out, so its tunnel and chute are 0.24 longer
and its vector_to_place_result is re-measured; N, E, W unchanged.
Chute, alternative: over the wall
ore falls 1.13
inclined drag chain on the plate top;
the head over the wall's edge
the ore must first be lifted 0.85 inside the press
The chain shows from the camera on every face, but: the spec's chute
(ground level, sloping down and forward out of the deck) is replaced; the
ore must be lifted inside the press; it falls about 1.1 to the ground, so
the ore particles and vector_to_place_result are redone in all four
directions; and the chute crosses the plate top where the hoses of other
directions run (the E/W hoses' lanes).
Questions for Liam
Q1 Chute with the bays closed: (a) through a port in the wall at ground level, as the spec's chute, with its drive on the plate top to mark the output face [recommended, drawn];
(b) the same port, no drive on top (the output face then shows only on the south face and while ore falls); (c) over the wall (spec change; ore lifted and dropped ~1.1).
Q2 The idle faces' ports: shut by a flush bolted hatch on each (the body never turns) [recommended, drawn]; or the port drawn in the chute's own layer, blind wall elsewhere.
Q3 South face: the whole face out to 2.74 [drawn, as asked]; or a cast boss 0.24 proud round each south fitting only, the face between at the footprint edge (the south chute then unchanged).
Either way the south wall's foot draws 0.24 (15 px at 1x) past the footprint's edge, as the end rings did.
Q4 Hose ends: a cast boss on the plate against the shoulder, the nozzle down into it [drawn]; the ring's landing radius (1.30) leaves the shoulder's 0.10 rim too narrow for a 0.32 hose.
